slot.brief: A ball strikes a smooth surface obliquely and rebounds; use momentum components along and normal to the wall with a given coefficient of restitution to find rebound speed and angle.

stem: A ball strikes a smooth horizontal floor at $2\sqrt{6}$ m s$^{-1}$, making an angle of $45^\circ$ with the floor. If the coefficient of restitution is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, its rebound speed and angle with the floor are

verdicts.working: Resolve the incident velocity: horizontal and vertical components are both $2\sqrt{3}$ m s$^{-1}$. The horizontal component is unchanged; the rebound vertical component is $e(2\sqrt{3})=2$ m s$^{-1}$. Thus speed $=\sqrt{(2\sqrt{3})^2+2^2}=4$ m s$^{-1}$ and angle $=\tan^{-1}(2/(2\sqrt{3}))=30^\circ$.

working:
$u_\parallel=u_\perp=2\sqrt{6}\cos45^\circ=2\sqrt{3}$ m s$^{-1}$
$v_\parallel=u_\parallel=2\sqrt{3}$ m s$^{-1}$
$v_\perp=e u_\perp=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(2\sqrt{3})=2$ m s$^{-1}$
$v=\sqrt{v_\parallel^2+v_\perp^2}=\sqrt{12+4}=4$ m s$^{-1}$
$\tan\theta=\dfrac{v_\perp}{v_\parallel}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\Rightarrow\theta=30^\circ$
